requirement_title: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.
requirement_text:
# REQ-2297: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2297
Type: feature

## Requirement

MessagePack generated code is not decorated with the `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage` attribute. Because it is very hard to write good coverage for generated MessagePack code, it may skew coverage numbers, especially on large projects with a lot of generated code.

Solution requested: "I would like all generated code to be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.  I do not feel like a setting is needed, but setting would be fine to have too."

Alternatives considered by the author: none; "it is close to impossible to write good coverage for generated code as it covers many edge cases."

## Acceptance criteria

- All generated code is decorated with `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`.
- No new setting or option is required to get the attribute. ("I do not feel like a setting is needed")
- An opt-out setting would be acceptable but is optional. ("setting would be fine to have too")
- The generated code still compiles on every supported target framework (the attribute must exist there or be conditionally emitted). (derived)
- Existing verified generator snapshots are updated to include the attribute. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- b-kurczynski-dl suggests a coverage-tool workaround instead: exclude `obj\\.*\.g\.cs$` in the `dotnet-coverage` settings XML.
- armadavalor offers a PR: add `[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` (and possibly `GeneratedCode`) to the types emitted by the templates under `src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/` (formatters, string-key formatters, enum/union formatters, resolvers), update the verified snapshots, no setting. Asks AArnott whether he would accept it or prefer to point users at coverage-tool configuration. No maintainer reply in the thread.
- Ambiguity driver: scope (all generated types vs formatters only) and setting (unconditional vs opt-out) are both open.

findings.claim: Enum formatters use the inverse target-framework condition from every other template. Consequently, on modern targets such as net8.0 the enum formatter's ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute is inactive, so not all generated code is decorated. On NETSTANDARD2_0 or NETFRAMEWORK it is instead active even though the change identifies those as targets where the attribute is unavailable, breaking the supported-target compilation criterion there.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.EnumExcludeFromCodeCoverageRequirementTests.EnumFormatter_HasActiveExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttributeOnModernTargets. It parses the generated enum formatter with modern-target preprocessor symbols and fails on head because the attribute occurs only inside inactive '#if NETSTANDARD2_0 || NETFRAMEWORK' text. Additionally, compiling that generated formatter with NETSTANDARD2_0 against netstandard2.0 references exercises the reversed availability branch.

hunches.claim: The enum formatter's preprocessor condition is inverted. On modern targets, including .NET 8, the generated EnumFormatter has no ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute, while NETSTANDARD2_0 and NETFRAMEWORK are the only targets where the attribute is emitted. This misses enum formatters in the requested coverage and risks using the attribute on precisely the legacy targets for which every other template suppresses it.

receipt_plan.detail: Generate a formatter for an enum referenced by a MessagePackObject using normal .NET 8 preprocessor symbols and inspect the active attributes on the generated enum formatter class. EnumFormatter_IsExcludedFromCodeCoverage_OnModernTargets demonstrates that ExcludeFromCodeCoverage is absent.

hunches.claim: Applying ExcludeFromCodeCoverage unconditionally to the generated partial resolver causes CS0579 when the consumer has already applied the same attribute to their partial resolver declaration. Attributes from partial declarations are combined, and ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute does not allow multiples, so existing user workarounds become compile errors.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile a [GeneratedMessagePackResolver] partial class that is also annotated with [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]. ResolverWithUserSuppliedCoverageAttributeStillCompiles expects no generated-code compilation diagnostics and fails on head with the duplicate-attribute error.

hunches.claim: Enum formatters use the inverse framework condition from every other template: the attribute is emitted only for NETSTANDARD2_0/NETFRAMEWORK and omitted on modern target frameworks. Consequently, enum generated code is not decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage for those targets.

receipt_plan.detail: Regenerate the source-generator snapshots for an enum formatter on a modern target (for example net8.0) and on netstandard2.0; verify that the modern output contains [global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] on the formatter and that EnumTemplate.cs and EnumTemplate.tt use the same condition.

hunches.claim: The enum formatter template reverses the target-framework guard: it emits ExcludeFromCodeCoverage only for NETSTANDARD2_0 or NETFRAMEWORK, where the attribute is unavailable, and omits it on other targets. This breaks enum formatter coverage exclusion on modern targets and can make generated enum formatters fail to compile on the older targets.

receipt_plan.detail: Run CodeCoverageExclusionTests.ExcludeAttributeIsGuardedForTargetsWhereItIsUnavailable; the generated enum formatter contains the attribute behind '#if NETSTANDARD2_0 || NETFRAMEWORK', so its guardedCount is zero and the assertion fails. Also inspect that generated enum source: the preprocessor symbol must be negated to match the other templates.

hunches.claim: The new tests do not exercise EnumTemplate, so its inverted preprocessor condition survives: the attribute is emitted only on NETSTANDARD2_0/NETFRAMEWORK instead of being excluded there. MyEnum is not referenced by any generated formatter input, so neither test inspects enum output.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/EnumTemplate.tt:9 negate-condition: #if NETSTANDARD2_0 || NETFRAMEWORK -> #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK; expected to survive because the test's standalone, unreferenced MyEnum produces no enum formatter, leaving EnumTemplate output unexamined.

hunches.claim: The tests check only that each generated file contains at least one guarded attribute, not that every generated type has one. Removing the attribute from FormatterCache (and likewise the resolver's GetFormatterHelper) leaves both the per-file containment assertion and the equal attribute/guard counts passing.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/ResolverTemplate.tt:32 delete-statement: [global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] -> remove the attribute and its guard; expected to survive because the enclosing resolver class still supplies the one attribute required by AllGeneratedTypesAreExcludedFromCodeCoverage, and ExcludeAttributeIsGuardedForTargetsWhereItIsUnavailable only compares file-wide counts.

hunches.claim: The TransformUtilities constrained-nesting newline change has no coverage in the added test source, which contains no nested generic types with constraints. Restoring the old constrained branch would not affect any output inspected by these tests.

residual_risk: This change touches 237 files (222 generated) in codegen-templates, tests; the highest routed risk is 7/10. 14 file(s) were routed for deep review, 1 for light review and 222 to the regeneration check. The existing source generator tests ran on head: 160 of 169 passed, 9 failed. 7 unverified hunch(es) remain without an executed receipt. It touches risky areas (codegen-templates), so a human must sign off. 6 thing(s) were not checked, including mutation testing; generated formatter bytes (source generator output, base vs head); compatibility byte diff (base vs head serialized bytes). By signing off, the signer accepts any defect that only those unchecked paths would have revealed. The change is blocked; signing off is not offered until the blocker is fixed.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Decorate every generated type—including formatters, string-key formatters, enum/union formatters, and resolvers—with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage unconditionally and provide no setting. Code: Update all relevant source-generator transforms so every emitted generated type receives the attribute, conditionally emitting it only as needed for target-framework compatibility, and update all affected verified snapshots; unlike the narrower reading, resolver and other non-formatter generated types are included, and unlike the opt-out reading no configuration API is added.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Apply ExcludeFromCodeCoverage unconditionally only to generated formatter types, leaving non-formatter generated code such as resolvers without the attribute. Code: Change the formatter-related transforms and their snapshots but not resolver or other generated-type templates; the emitted coverage behavior and scope of modified snapshots differ from the all-generated-types reading.
